deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Riemann. It is part of a letter dated 'den 25ten', signed on the next page by H. A. Schwarz. The addressee is almost certainly Heinrich Weber, the editor of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The letter concerns the proof sheet ('Bogen 20') of Hattendorff's redaction of Riemann's memoir 'Ueber die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung'. Why the letter sits in the Riemann bundle 'R.Minimal' is presumably because of this editorial context.

(a) Personal and academic matters. Frau Clebsch sends a photograph of the late Alfred Clebsch (died 1872) for Neumann's album. Neumann is presumably Franz Neumann, Weber's teacher; he is an auswärtiges Mitglied of the Göttingen Society. Schwarz asks for the date of Neumann's jubilee so that Wöhler can send a congratulatory letter in the Society's name.

(b) Editorial criticism. Schwarz disagrees with the redaction in many places on sheet 20 but says it is too late to change it. He adds that others are also dissatisfied with Hattendorff's editing of Riemann.

(c) Article 18. Schwarz would not have objected if a note had said that one can actually derive, from the given equations for X, Y, Z, a finished equation between x, y, z. X, Y, Z are presumably the normal or direction cosines of the parametric representation.

(d) Article 19 (minimal surfaces swept out by circles in parallel planes, i.e. Riemann's minimal surfaces). Schwarz complains that the geometric meaning of the laboriously derived equations is never stated.

Example, p. 312: the relations alpha = -a*m + d, beta = -b*m + c. Reading that is mine and uncertain: alpha and beta are presumably the rates of change dx0/dz and dy0/dz of the circle centre (x0, y0) with height z, both affine in one auxiliary quantity m. Eliminating m gives the linear relation b*alpha - a*beta = b*d - a*c. Integrating in z, the centres satisfy b*x0 - a*y0 - (b*d - a*c)*z = const. So the curve of centres is a plane curve. Schwarz adds, without proof here, that this plane is a symmetry plane of the surface.

Second point: Hattendorff (following Riemann) derives the addition theorem of elliptic integrals but draws no geometric consequence. Schwarz proposes the conclusion, inserted tentatively with a question mark: under the conformal map of the surface to the sphere (the Gauss map), the family of circles corresponds to a family of confocal spherical conics.

The page contains no derivations, only remarks about what should have been stated.
errors: No mathematical errors can be judged: no derivations are carried out. The step from 'plane curve' to 'symmetry plane' is asserted without argument; it is true for Riemann's minimal surfaces but not shown here.
The confocal spherical conics claim is explicitly tentative ('?') in the manuscript.

results.what: The centres of the circles foliating a minimal surface swept out by circles in parallel planes lie on a plane curve, and that plane is a symmetry plane of the surface.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a letter by H. A. Schwarz, not Riemann, giving editorial criticism of Hattendorff's edition. It is historically interesting for the Werke editing process. The mathematical content consists of geometric glosses on Riemann's known 1867 results; the spherical-conic remark is mildly interesting but tentative.

checkable.asserts: If dx0/dz=alpha and dy0/dz=beta, the centres (x0,y0,z) lie in a fixed plane b*x - a*y - (b*d-a*c)*z = const.

transcription_corrections: 'auf so sehr mühsamen Weise' is probably 'auf so sehr mühsame Weise' in the manuscript.
'in einer Anmerkung' is an interlinear insertion belonging after 'am Schluße'.
'moniert' may be spelled 'monirt' in the 19th-century orthography.
